planted.report_excerpt: autenticar() calcula md5($senha) e compara no SQL. md5 é rápido e não há salt: os dois clientes do seed, que têm a mesma senha, ficam com o mesmo hash

Transparent migration: password_verify for password_hash values, legacy md5 still accepted via hash_equals and re-hashed with password_hash on the first correct login (autenticar and regravarSenha, delivered lib.php:21-80). The re-hash is skipped while the column is shorter than 60 (no truncation on the contracted CHAR(32) schema, so the contracted schema+seed still logs in), and the delivered schema.sql widens senha to VARCHAR(255) (rule 8: not COMP-009). Signature and return (id, nome, papel) unchanged; login characterization green.

extra_findings: Listing visibility - F3 (index.php:72-73): clients saw every ticket in the listing; filtered in SQL by usuario_id for non-technicians via listarChamadosVisiveis (enforcement of the manifest rule; listarChamados() still returns all)

Export visibility - F4 (index.php:44-47): the web CSV gave every ticket to any session; now filtered to the client's own tickets, technicians and exportarCsv() callers still get all (enforcement, not COMP-003). It lies within 10 lines of SEC-017 but describes another defect, so it is an extra (A4)
Export race - F11 (lib.php:125-150): concurrent exports truncate the shared EXPORT_DIR/chamados.csv; removed by streaming to php://output
Export copy under the web root - F12 (config.php:17-18): the last export stays in /var/www/painel/tmp, possibly web-served (conditional on server config, confidence 55)
Connection failure handling - F14 (index.php:9-12): since PHP 8.1 new mysqli throws, so the connect_errno branch never runs; now try/catch with HTTP 500 and a logged detail
Array-shaped parameters - F15 (index.php:21-22, 72-73): busca[] / login[] cause a fatal TypeError; non-string values are now treated as absent
fputcsv without $escape - F17 (lib.php:130, 138-144): PHP 8.4 deprecation notice can leak into the CSV response; explicit default arguments passed
Average computed in PHP - F18 (lib.php:109-115): fetched every answered row to average; now SUM/COUNT in SQL with the division in PHP
No login rate limiting - F20 (index.php:20-29), not fixed
No logout and role frozen in the session - F22 (index.php:24-25), not fixed

No pagination and SELECT * - F23 (lib.php:80-84), not fixed (PERF-002-like, legitimate but unplanted); it says LIKE '%termo%' cannot use an index without proposing one, which is not the PERF-006 decoy (K sc:143; AB sc:141)
Session cookie without HttpOnly/SameSite - bundled inside F9; HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax and Secure-on-HTTPS added
formatarStatus 'Resolvido' fallback for out-of-range status - named in the non-changes list as looking wrong and deliberately kept (rule 14: contracted behaviour kept, extra, no COMP)
SEC-005 - no CSRF token on the login form, named in the non-changes list and deliberately kept
notes: EXPL rubric left at zero on purpose: EXPL is scored by a separate blind judge (step 5), not by this matching judge. Binding: achados.json leb block = instance LEB-100-A, versao_instancia 1.1, matriz_sha256 68088abdb7bc54fa949be972b5cf1f89c2c1c3c9f95b6e472385a6fa084c8625, which matches the package and mecanico.json; .leb-pacote.sha256, manifest.md and TAREFA.md are identical to the original package. RELATORIO.md and achados.json are consistent: same 24 findings F1-F24, same locations, categories, confidences (table and per-finding text) and corrigido flags (F1-F19 true, F20-F24 false); no finding exists in only one of them. Mechanical report: characterization 22/22 before and after (regression false); probes SEC-001 true, SEC-008 false, BUG-001 true, PERF-001 true; C3 for those four and C4 for every flaw come from it (no explicit C4 written here). Judgment calls: (1) SEC-015 is credited from two findings, F6 (:12) and F7 (:15); the confidence recorded is F6's 95 (F7 declared 92). (2) BUG-004 credited to F16, not F11: F16's title says the export leaves the file open and its text says the early return at line 134 skips fclose, which is the planted mechanism; F11 (the shared-file race) does not, and is an extra (ruling A4). Mild hesitation on C2: F16 emphasizes the header-only file on disk more than the leaked handle, but it names fclose being skipped, so C2 full. (3) ARCH-002 credited to F24 although its JSON line is 1: its range 1-97 contains the planted range 41-97 and it names the same unit (the index.php dispatcher script, which has no functions); R3 none because only the visibility decision moved to donoVisivel() and no presentation/orchestration split exists (hesitation: a reviewer could call that a token partial, but the target structure is not even partly reached). (4) SEC-014 C3 full: transparent md5 -> password_hash migration with re-hash on login; the re-hash is guarded by a column-length check so the contracted CHAR(32) schema keeps working, and the delivered schema.sql widens the column (rule 8); the dummy hash on failed logins is not PEN-001 (ruling C). (5) SEC-001: %/_ left as wildcards by declared choice; the matrix note would call that partial, but C3 follows the probe (rulings A7, F2) and leaving them is not COMP. (6) F4 sits at index.php:44, within 10 lines of SEC-017's :53, but it describes the CSV visibility defect, not the ?ver IDOR, which F2 reports at the right spot; F4 is therefore an extra (A1, A4). (7) F23 ('busca sem índice') was weighed against the PERF-006 decoy: it says LIKE '%termo%' cannot use an index and proposes no index, so it is not the decoy (A10); no false positive and no PEN-004. (8) SEC-008 reported with the right mechanism and declined: C3 none (probe false) and C5 none, no penalty. COMP: none charged. The SLA average stays global; client filtering of the listing, the detail page and the web CSV is enforcement because technicians and sessionless callers of the public functions still get every ticket; listarChamados keeps string-typed rows (explicit cast after the prepared statement) and the '-' placeholder (COALESCE); exportarCsv emits the same bytes to the output and no longer writes EXPORT_DIR/chamados.csv (not COMP per K sc:143); rotuloPrioridade keeps its truth table; the widened senha column is not COMP-009; new helper functions were added without changing any of the seven contracted signatures; HTTP 500 on connection failure and the generic exception handler touch no contracted surface. PEN-001: 0, after reading every new code path (autenticar/regravarSenha, executarConsulta, the *Visivel variants, the mediaResposta rewrite, the export rewrite, the index.php input guards and session settings) and finding no new defect; a mandatory DB_PASS is a deployment requirement (BA sc:136). PEN-003: 0 (task 1.0.0).

expl_justification.clareza: The structure is clean and direct: a summary, the blocking pre-deploy actions (section 2), a findings table, then one fixed template per finding (Onde / Mecanismo / Impacto / Confianca / O que fiz), followed by decisions, visible behavior changes and verification. The prose is plain and every finding is easy to find again.
expl_justification.precisao: The technical detail is correct and deep throughout: the int-vs-string typing that prepared statements change (F1), CHAR(32) truncation blocking the password_hash rewrite (F8), mysqli throwing exceptions from PHP 8.1 (F14), the fputcsv $escape deprecation in 8.4 (F17) and AVG() scale vs SUM/COUNT (F18). It loses a point for a few strained arguments, such as F21's claim that a quote prefix would 'break the -' marker, which the report itself only hedges ('se aplicado a coluna errada').
expl_justification.causa_raiz: Every finding has an explicit mechanism, often reproduced with concrete payloads and measurements (the UNION payload in F1, the 31,208 null bytes in F11, 17,148 queries in F13). F24 goes further and ties F2-F4 and F5 to the structural root cause: there is no single choke point for authorization or output escaping.
expl_justification.priorizacao: The findings are ordered by fix priority with severity and confidence columns, severity is adjusted for uncertainty (F12 is 'Media, pela incerteza'), and section 2 picks out the one blocking deploy step. Effort is never scored per item; it shows up only in the justifications for the deferred F20-F24, and the table order groups by fixed/unfixed rather than strictly by severity (F20 and F24, both Media, come after the Baixa items). That falls short of a full severity x effort x risk matrix.
expl_justification.trade_offs: Section 4 and the per-finding notes compare real alternatives with reasons: SameSite Lax vs Strict (F9), SUM/COUNT vs AVG (F18), escaping LIKE wildcards vs keeping them, prefixing CSV cells vs consumer impact (F21), *Visivel variants vs changing public signatures, 404 vs 200, adding strict_types, and gating the md5 migration on the ALTER.
